functions.name: cartesian_product<T>::iterator::operator*
functions.description: Dereferences the iterator to produce the current tuple (combination) in the cartesian product as a std::vector<T>. The returned reference refers to internal storage that is rebuilt on each dereference and advanced on increment. Typical usage: iterate with for (auto it = cp.begin(); it != cp.end(); ++it) { auto& tuple = *it; ... }.
requirements: The iterator must be in a valid (non-end) state; dereferencing the end iterator is undefined behavior (inferred from iterator semantics).
The returned reference becomes invalid after the next call to operator*() or operator++() because the internal buffer is cleared and rebuilt.

The underlying input vectors referenced by the cartesian_product must remain valid and not be modified in a way that invalidates their iterators during iteration (inferred from storing const_iterators into the input vectors).

functions.name: cartesian_product<T>::iterator::operator++
functions.description: Advances the iterator to the next tuple in the cartesian product sequence. When all combinations are exhausted, the iterator becomes equal to end().
requirements: operator++ must not be called on the end iterator (inferred from typical forward-iterator requirements; doing so would wrap internal state unexpectedly).
The underlying input vectors must remain valid and not be structurally modified during iteration, or iterator invalidation may occur (inferred from use of const_iterators).

functions.name: cartesian_product<T>::iterator::operator==
functions.description: Compares two iterators for equality. Iterators compare equal when they are at the same logical position (including both being end).
requirements: Only compare iterators that originate from the same cartesian_product instance; comparing iterators from different ranges is undefined by convention and this implementation compares only an internal position marker (inferred from standard iterator requirements and implementation).

functions.name: cartesian_product<T>::begin
functions.description: Returns an iterator positioned at the first tuple of the cartesian product of the provided vector-of-vectors. If any inner vector is empty, begin() will equal end().
requirements: The cartesian_product instance must have been constructed with a reference to a vector-of-vectors that remains alive for the duration of any iteration.
The contained vectors should not be modified in a way that invalidates their iterators while iterating (inferred).

functions.name: cartesian_product<T>::end
functions.description: Returns a sentinel end iterator used to compare for completion of iteration over the cartesian product.
requirements: Only use end() for comparison; dereferencing or incrementing the end iterator is undefined behavior (inferred from iterator semantics).

functions.name: cartesian_product_size
functions.signature: template <typename T> size_t cartesian_product_size(const std::vector<std::vector<T>>& vec_of_vecs)
functions.description: Computes the total number of combinations in the cartesian product by multiplying the sizes of all inner vectors. Note: if vec_of_vecs is empty, the function returns 1 (product of zero factors), which may or may not match higher-level expectations.
requirements: Callers must be aware that size_t multiplication may overflow silently for large inputs; the function does not check for overflow.
The input container may be empty and inner vectors may be empty; behavior is as implemented (returns 1 for empty outer vector, and 0 if any inner vector is empty).

functions.name: cartesian_product_is_empty
functions.signature: template <typename T> bool cartesian_product_is_empty(const std::vector<std::vector<T>>& vec_of_vecs)
functions.description: Returns true if the cartesian product would produce no tuples: either the outer vector is empty or at least one inner vector is empty. Otherwise returns false.
requirements: None beyond providing a valid reference to a vector of vectors; the function performs only reads.

functions.name: make_cartesian_product
functions.signature: template <typename T> cartesian_product<T> make_cartesian_product(const std::vector<std::vector<T>>& vec_of_vecs)
functions.description: Convenience factory that constructs a cartesian_product<T> range over the given vector-of-vectors without specifying the template argument explicitly.
requirements: The passed vector-of-vectors must outlive the returned cartesian_product<T> object and any iterators obtained from it, because the cartesian_product stores a const reference.
Callers should not modify the underlying vectors in a way that invalidates iterators while iterating (inferred).
